Statements: Some files are branches. All branches are tokens. No tokens is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are tokens.
II. Some branches are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are branches. Some branches are tokens. All tokens are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. No branches is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are branches. All branches are tokens. No tokens is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not branches.
II. No branches is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. Some cheques are branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings credit access = ni lu su
savings digital growth = vo su re
credit digital banking = vo lu mi
access growth banking = re ni mi
savings credit banking = mi su lu
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ni. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = su, credit = lu, access = ni, digital = vo, growth = re, banking = mi.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 39 km east, turns left and walks 45 km, then turns left and walks 15 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 24 km along the initial direction and 45 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(24² + 45²) = 51 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 96 km north, turns right and walks 180 km, then turns right and walks 21 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 195. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 75 km along the initial direction and 180 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(75² + 180²) = 195 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 90 km south, turns right and walks 135 km, then turns right and walks 18 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 153. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 72 km along the initial direction and 135 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(72² + 135²) = 153 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of D. C is the daughter of D. E is the father of D. How is C related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. E is a parent of D, and C is D’s daughter. Hence C is E’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of A. A is the mother of C. F is the father of G and A. How is G related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of C’s mother A. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of D. D is the father of F. E is the son of F. C is the sister of D. How is D related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of F, and F is E’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. New front rank = 14+3 = 17. Back rank = 43 − 17 + 1 = 27.

questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. New front rank = 10+4 = 14. Back rank = 47 − 14 + 1 = 34.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3300 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 20% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6875. Recover each cost separately: 3300×100/120 + 3300×100/80. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 64 and 96 hours. An outlet empties it in 160 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 50.53. Net rate = 1/64 + 1/96 − 1/160 = 19/960 tank/hour. Required time = 50.53 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 170 km in still water in 10 hours. If the stream flows at 2 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 75. Still-water speed = 17 km/h. Upstream speed = 17 − 2. Distance = speed × 5.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:4. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹115200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 158400. Profit ratio is 96:36. Each ratio unit = ₹1200. Total = 132 × 1200.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹15000 earns ₹6750 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 19837.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 15000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 160 litres of pure milk. 32 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 102.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 160 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 28 people is 43 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 72. New total minus old total = (28+1)×(43+1) − 28×43 = 72.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 14 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+14)/(x+14) = 3/2 gives x = 14. Present sum = 3x.
